subject: Quantitative Aptitude (QA)
source_note: Compiled from CAT 2025 (conducted 30 Nov 2025 by IIM Kozhikode) slot-wise analyses and multi-year (2021-2025) coaching-tracker PYQ weightage data, cross-checked Sep 2026. CAT has no officially published syllabus document; topic lists here reflect NCERT Class 9-10-level mathematics as consistently tested across recent years' papers. Always cross-check against the current-year CAT official notification/mock test.
exam_pattern_note: CAT QA: 22 questions, 40-minute fixed time limit, no sectional choice. No sub-sections within QA (unlike DILR's set structure). Typically 14-17 MCQs and 5-8 TITA questions per slot.

subtopics: Time, Speed and Distance (including races, trains, boats/streams)
Time and Work (including pipes and cisterns)
topics.note: Consistently the single largest QA topic group across 2021-2025 (~40-42% of the section).

subtopics: Sequences, series and progressions (AP, GP, HP)
topics.note: Second-largest topic group (~30-32% across 2021-2025); functions/graphs and progressions are the sub-topics most likely to be perceived as 'hard'.

subtopics: Mensuration: area and volume of 2D/3D figures
topics.note: ~14-18% of the section across 2021-2025; steady but consistently smaller than Arithmetic/Algebra.
~9-10% of the section; fewer questions but each often conceptually dense.
Smallest QA topic group (~2-9%, varies notably year to year); low volume but often high scoring-efficiency per question for well-prepared candidates.
